title: Advice to young musicians: study the fundamentals
summary: She urges thorough study, written work, scales, harmony and sight reading rather than playing right away, and credits her first teacher.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Is there anything else that you'd like to add about your life in music? Any advice that you'd have for any younger musicians coming up?

Well, it takes a lot of study, I can say that. But the young people don't want to study. That's right. They want to begin playing right away. But I still like that method of catechism and written work and all those sort of things. And when you're learning music. It has paid off for me. I wouldn't give anything for it. But of course the music pupils of today want to go right to the piano and begin playing. But how are you going to play if you don't know the basic things about music? So my advice would be to learn correctly. Have the right start. Anything that is done right where you can't help but make a success of it. But if you just try to run through something, you're going to lose something along the way. So I still believe in that written work and the catechism and the scales by all means. Because it gives dexterity. And I like sight reading, improvisation and things like that. Harmony. All of those things are essential. But they go in now for just playing. They don't care whether they have harmony or not. But I don't like that sort of playing. And as I said before, I owe everything to my first teacher.
